obligations.title: Risk management system
obligations.detail: Set up, document and maintain a risk management process for the whole lifecycle of the system.

citation.title: Risk management system

obligations.title: Data and data governance
obligations.detail: Training, validation and test data must follow data governance practices fit for the purpose, including checks for bias.

citation.title: Data and data governance

obligations.title: Technical documentation
obligations.detail: Draw up the technical documentation before the system goes on the market and keep it up to date.

citation.title: Technical documentation

obligations.title: Record keeping

citation.label: Article 12(1)
citation.title: Record-keeping

obligations.title: Human oversight by design
obligations.detail: Build the system so recruiters can oversee it effectively while it is in use.

citation.title: Human oversight

obligations.title: Use as instructed

citation.title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
citation.quote: Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure they use such systems in accordance with the instructions for use

obligations.title: Assign human oversight
obligations.detail: Give oversight to people with the competence, training and authority to do it.

citation.label: Article 26(2)
citation.title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
citation.quote: Deployers shall assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support.

open_questions.question: Does a recruiter review every ranking before a candidate is rejected?
open_questions.why: Human review does not remove the high-risk class, but it shapes how Article 14 and Article 26 are met.

open_questions.question: Does the tool only sort applications by a fixed rule, such as the date received?
open_questions.why: A narrow procedural task could fall under the Article 6(3) exemption.

open_questions.question: Are the applicants in the European Union?
open_questions.why: The Act applies when the output is used in the Union, even if the provider is outside it.

summary: A software service that reads job applications, ranks candidates against a vacancy and shows recruiters a shortlist of the top applicants.
headline: Ranking job applicants is an Annex III employment use, so the system is high-risk under Article 6(2).

steps.title: Scope
steps.question: Is this an AI system that falls under the Act?
steps.reasoning: The tool infers from the applications it receives how to rank candidates, which fits the definition of an AI system. The provider places it on the Union market, so the Act applies.

citations.label: Article 3(1)
citations.title: Definitions
citations.quote: ‘AI system’ means a machine-based system that is designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy

citations.label: Article 2(1)
citations.title: Scope
citations.quote: providers placing on the market or putting into service AI systems or placing on the market general-purpose AI models in the Union

steps.title: Prohibited practices
steps.question: Is it a prohibited AI practice under Article 5?
steps.reasoning: Nothing in the description points to manipulation, social scoring, emotion recognition at work or any other Article 5 practice.

citations.label: Article 5(1)
citations.title: Prohibited AI practices
citations.quote: the use of AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions

steps.title: High-risk classification
steps.question: Is it high-risk under Article 6(1) with Annex I or Article 6(2) with Annex III?
steps.reasoning: Filtering applications and evaluating candidates is listed word for word in Annex III, point 4(a). Article 6(2) makes every Annex III system high-risk unless the exemption applies.

citations.label: Article 6(2)
citations.title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
citations.quote: AI systems referred to in Annex III shall be considered to be high-risk.

citations.label: Annex III, point 4
citations.title: High-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2)
citations.quote: to analyse and filter job applications, and to evaluate candidates

steps.title: Article 6(3) exemption
steps.question: Does the Article 6(3) exemption take it out of the high-risk class?
steps.reasoning: The ranking shapes who gets an interview, so it materially influences the outcome of a decision. It is not a narrow procedural task. A system that profiles natural persons is always high-risk.

citations.label: Article 6(3)
citations.title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
citations.quote: including by not materially influencing the outcome of decision making

citations.label: Article 6(3)
citations.title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
citations.quote: an AI system referred to in Annex III shall always be considered high-risk where the AI system performs profiling of all natural persons

steps.title: Transparency duties
steps.question: Do the Article 50 transparency obligations apply?
steps.reasoning: Candidates do not talk to the system and it does not generate synthetic content, so Article 50 adds no separate duty here.

steps.title: General-purpose AI
steps.question: Is a general-purpose AI model provided, with Chapter V obligations?
steps.reasoning: The description does not say the tool is a general-purpose model or is built on one.

deadlines.label: The AI Act enters into force
deadlines.detail: Article 113: the Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day after its publication in the Official Journal (12 July 2024). Entry into force is not the same as application: most rules apply later, see the dates below.

deadlines.label: Prohibited practices and AI literacy apply
deadlines.detail: Article 113, third paragraph, point (a): Chapters I and II (general provisions including Article 4 AI literacy, and the Article 5 prohibitions) apply from 2 February 2025, except Article 5(1), points (ba) and (bb), and Article 5(1a) and (1b), which apply from 2 December 2026. Article 4 in its current wording (support the development of AI literacy) applies since Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 entered into force on 27 July 2026.

deadlines.label: Penalty rules apply
deadlines.detail: Article 113, third paragraph, point (b): Chapter XII (penalties) applies from 2 August 2025. Breaking an Article 5 prohibition can be fined up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher (Article 99(3)); breaches of other duties, including Articles 16, 26 and 50, up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3 % (Article 99(4)). For SMEs and start-ups the lower of the two amounts applies (Article 99(6)); for SMCs the lower amount applies to the fines of paragraphs 4 and 5 (Article 99(6a)).

deadlines.label: Digital Omnibus on AI enters into force
deadlines.detail: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 July 2026, published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026, enters into force on the third day after publication (its Article 4). From this date Articles 102 to 110 apply (Article 113, third paragraph, point (d)), and the amended provisions that have no later date, such as Article 4 and Article 4a, apply. It moves the high-risk dates, adds two prohibitions from 2 December 2026 and adds a transition period for Article 50(2).

deadlines.label: General date of application
deadlines.detail: Article 113, second paragraph: the Regulation applies from 2 August 2026, except where Article 113 sets another date. This includes Chapter IV (Article 50 transparency duties) and Article 101 (fines for general-purpose AI model providers). Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 (high-risk classification, requirements and obligations) no longer apply from this date: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 moved them, see the high-risk entries.

deadlines.label: Transparency duties of Article 50 apply
deadlines.detail: Article 50 is in Chapter IV, which follows the general date of application in Article 113. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 did not move this date; it only added a later date for Article 50(2) marking by systems already on the market (next entry). A high-risk system can carry Article 50 duties as well (Article 50(6)).

deadlines.label: High-risk rules apply to Annex III systems
deadlines.detail: Article 113, third paragraph, point (c)(i): Chapter III Sections 1, 2 and 3 (except Article 6(5)) apply from 2 December 2027 to AI systems classified as high-risk under Article 6(2) and Annex III. The original 2024 text set 2 August 2026; Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 moved it. Systems placed on the market or put into service before this date are covered only if their design changes significantly afterwards (Article 111(2)), except systems for public authorities (2 August 2030).
